messages:
Anya: Starting a KV-only quantization kernel sweep (FP8 vs INT8) across rinf-7b and rinf-13b. Goal: measure cold p95, warm p95, sustained throughput, per-token kernel overhead, and KV memory footprint. Using seq_len=256 for these runs to stress cache behavior. Posting a short summary here.
Ben: Nice. What do you mean by cold vs warm in this sweep?
Anya: Definitions: cold = fresh process + empty KV cache; warm = after ~100 sequences to populate typical KV patterns. Config I used: 
```
./perf/kv_quant_bench.py \n  --models rinf-7b,rinf-13b \n  --quant-schemes fp8,int8 \n  --kv-only \n  --batch-sizes 1,4,8 \n  --seq-len 256 \n  --warm-iter 100 \n  --measure p95,throughput,kv_mem,perplexity,kernel_times 
```
Chris: Please paste the CSV or a quick table. :eyes:
Anya: Quick aggregated CSV excerpt (cold/warm p95 in ms, KV mem in MB, perp delta vs fp32):
```
Model,Quant,Batch,p95_cold_ms,p95_warm_ms,kv_mem_mb,perp_delta
rinf-7b,FP8,1,195,110,400,+0.35%
rinf-7b,INT8,1,260,140,320,+0.92%
rinf-13b,FP8,1,285,155,820,+0.28%
rinf-13b,INT8,1,330,185,700,+0.75%
rinf-7b,FP8,8,150,75,400,+0.35%
rinf-7b,INT8,8,190,95,320,+0.92%
```
Mira: Interesting — INT8 gives better raw KV compression but larger cold latency. Any qualitative hits beyond perplexity?
Anya: Ran a focused 2k prompt QA/e2e eval and a token-level noise check. INT8 shows occasional token-level instability on long-context referential tasks (rare hallucination-like token swaps), EM on SQuAD-like sets unchanged within noise. FP8 is closer to fp32 across metrics. Full eval dashboard: https://internal.redwood/evals/kv-dequant-sweep-176994 (internal link).
Sam: How much runtime overhead are we seeing from dequant/reshape kernels on CUDA?
Anya: Captured kernel timings + memcpy breakdowns. Summary: INT8 path adds ~0.8-1.5 ms per token when dequantizing KV slices on A100, depending on alignment; FP8 path adds ~0.15-0.6 ms. Alignment and extra unpack ops for INT8 seem to be the main source. For batch=8 the amortized per-token penalty drops and INT8 can be competitive in throughput.
Ben: That explains cold p95 regression — first-time fills pay the alignment + decode cost that isn't amortized. Any hypothesis on why INT8 alignment hits are worse?
Anya: Two contributors: (1) our current INT8 kernel performs byte-unpacking + vectorized scaling in a separate kernel pass that forces an extra global sync for each KV write, (2) memory coalescing patterns are worse for INT8 layouts we generate from the quantizer. FP8 kernels use fused ops that avoid the extra pass.
Chris: Does batching hide it? For interactive small-batch workloads, FP8 looks safer?
Anya: Yes. Batch=1 interactive: FP8 wins on 95th latency. Batch>=4/8: INT8 throughput edges out FP8 for large working sets due to smaller KV footprint (more KV stays on-GPU).
Mira: Any proposal for production profiles and fallback logic?
Anya: Proposal draft:
- Profiles: `kv.fp8_interactive` (default for low-latency routes), `kv.int8_dense` (memory-optimized for heavy throughput/long-context workloads).
- Runtime flags: `--kv-quant-mode=[auto|fp8|int8|off]` and `--kv-quant-fallback-ms=TARGET` to trigger auto-fallback to fp32 or fp8 when p95 breaches SLO.
- Host gating: enable INT8 only on validated hardware labels (ga100,rtx6000-pro,ga100s).
- Canary strategy: short FP8 canary then INT8 canary behind capacity caps and perf monitors.
Sam: We should also gate by model size — maybe allow INT8 only for 13B+ where memory wins matter more?
Anya: Agree. My recommended default: 7B -> FP8 interactive, 13B+ -> INT8 optional behind gate.
Ben: What monitoring/telemetry do you want in the canary?
Anya: Need these metrics sent to console for canary windows: p95 cold/warm, per-token kernel times (dequant, unpack, memcpy), KV residency %, OOM count, and eval-quality smoke e2e (small constant prompt set). Also NVTX traces and perf flames saved for any run exceeding thresholds.
deploy-bot: Canary deploy scheduled: 2026-04-02 02:30 UTC -> cluster eng-infra-canary-3 (cap=6). Rollout plan: FP8 profile first (24h), INT8 gated canary after FP8 validation. :rocket:
Chris: Please run an extended overnight sweep with seq_len=1024 as well and include the NVTX + kernel histograms. Also add mixed prompt patterns (short, long, multi-turn).
Anya: Already queued seq=1024 job and mixed workload sweep for tonight. Will upload CSVs, kernel histograms, and a consolidated notebook with plots tomorrow AM.
Mira: If INT8 exhibits even small upticks in user-visible errors, we should have an immediate automated rollback.
Anya: Agreed. I'll add auto-rollback trigger if EM/e2e smoke error rate increases >2% or p95 spike >25% relative to baseline.
Ben: Thanks — and include raw kernel samples in the dump so the infra team can optimize the INT8 unpack pass.
Anya: Will attach NVTX traces, perf flames, and raw kernel timing CSVs. Ping me to join the canary window.
Sam: One more ask: can we expose a per-route override so customers on Dedicated can choose their preference?
Anya: Yep — exposing `kv_quant_mode` at route config is straightforward. I'll draft the API change in the PR.
Mira: Solid. Follow up after the overnight runs and we'll finalize rollout flags.
Anya: Will post results tomorrow. Thanks all.
